brief: A planter tower for a patio: one planter three storeys tall in the middle, ringed by six planters two storeys tall, with a crescent of five one-storey planters hugging the front of the ring on the side nearest the default view, so the whole build steps up one, two and three storeys away from the viewer. All bins radial-drain. Behind the ring, three one-storey cells with covers make a potting shelf: a seed tray on the first, a small nursery pot on each of the other two, each pot filled with soil and planted with a seedling. Fill every planter with soil and plant it: a patio tomato in the middle; butterhead lettuce, oakleaf lettuce, parsley, basil, chives and a marigold around the ring; nasturtium, alyssum, strawberry, thyme and oregano along the crescent. Use look to check that every plant is visible from the default view.

finish.summary: Built the stepped planter tower: 3-storey centre with patio tomato, 2-storey ring of six, 1-storey front crescent of five, all radial-drain bins soil-filled and planted as named, plus a three-cover potting shelf behind with seed tray and two soil-filled nursery pots with seedlings. check_build passes with meshClash clear. Two partials: the seed tray overhangs the rear of its cover (only placement the configurator accepted), and the back-left butterhead lettuce is occluded by the centre tower from the default view.

lines.label: Bin, full depth, drained, radial holes
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
